subject: BrightForge post-call: deployment synthesis, SLO targets & next steps
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Chen <laura@brightforge.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 09 Oct 2028 16:13:00 -0700
Subject: BrightForge post-call: deployment synthesis, SLO targets & next steps

Hi Laura — great to talk earlier. Quick recap from my side so we have alignment and clear next steps.

Pain points you emphasized:
- High tail latency during peak inference windows (95p reported spikes to ~1.2s) causing client timeouts and user retries.
- Cost unpredictability when traffic bursts hit daytime processing (batching currently disabled at app layer).
- Data residency: all inference for EU/US customers must stay in-region (you noted customers in US only for phase 1).
- Security/compliance: SOC2 evidence and audit logs required for procurement.

Goals you articulated:
- 95th percentile latency < 250ms for standard text generation (avg prompt length ~120 tokens, 2k context max).
- Sustained throughput target: 120 QPS peak with headroom for 250 QPS bursts.
- Deployment model: prefer Dedicated / Reserved capacity in US with private VPC and KMS integration.
- Success criteria for POC: meet latency SLO at 120 QPS sustained and show predictable cost per 1k tokens.

Technical notes we discussed (high level):
- Model family: you expect to run a 13B–33B open model (we discussed 13B FP16 and a quantized 33B variant).
- KV cache behavior: important for chat-like sessions; we'll preserve session affinity and hot-prefix caching.
- Autoscaling: recommend reserved baseline + burst pool to contain cost and meet spikes.

Immediate next steps (agreed):
1) I will share a proposed SLO matrix and suggested deployment topology (attached).
2) Karthik will run an initial micro-benchmark against sample prompt set (you to share anonymized sample prompts when ready).
3) Redwood to deliver a POC plan and cost estimate by Oct 16.
4) You to open an internal procurement ticket and share SOC2 requirements doc (if available).

Attachments: bf-slo-matrix-20281009.xlsx, bf-network-topology.png, call-recording-20281009.mp3

If anything above is incorrect or missing, please flag. Otherwise we plan to kick off the benchmark after you share the sample prompts (or a representative traffic CSV).

Thanks,
Connor

From: Laura Chen <laura@brightforge.ai>

Subject: Re: BrightForge post-call: deployment synthesis, SLO targets & next steps

Connor — thanks for the clear recap. Accurate capture; two clarifications:
1) The 95p spike we mentioned (1.2s) happens for long context sessions (1800–2000 tokens) under burst traffic — shorter sessions are usually fine.
2) For the POC we can provide a small sample set (anonymized) and a short synthetic traffic trace that imitates daily peak patterns.

Procurement has requested an initial SOC2 evidence packet (scope: infra/production) — I attached the internal request (sending separately via our procurement portal). We aim to decide on vendor shortlist by end of month.

Next: will share sample prompts + trace by EOD Thu (Oct 11). Please include a one-page POC scope when you respond.

— Laura
Head of Platform Engineering | BrightForge
laura@brightforge.ai
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, Laura Chen <laura@brightforge.ai>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Oct 2028 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: BrightForge post-call: deployment synthesis, SLO targets & next steps — initial tech readout

Laura / Connor — adding a short technical readout from the call and what I'd like to validate in the POC.

Observations from notes:
- Prompt distribution: median prompt ~120 tokens, tail to ~2000 (you confirmed). That distribution suggests latency variance will correlate strongly with requested context length and KV-cache hit rates.
- Model choices: 13B FP16 will likely meet 95p < 250ms at lower context lengths, but for sessions with 1.8–2k context we should test a quantized 33B variant with KV cache optimization.

POC validation matrix (what we'll measure):
- 95p & 99p latency across three traffic slices (low: 10–20 QPS, mid: 120 QPS sustained, high-burst: 250 QPS for 60s bursts).
- Cost per 1k tokens at observed batching levels and with auto-prefix cache enabled.
- Memory/KV pressure: observe memory utilization and KV eviction rate for long-context sessions.
- Fallback behavior: test automated routing to smaller model under resource pressure and measure user-visible degradation.

Recommended initial topology (attached diagram):
- Dedicated pool (US-west region) with 4x A100-equivalent machines as baseline and a 2-node burst pool.
- Private VPC peering + customer-controlled KMS for encryption-at-rest.
- Canary routing policy for canarying new model quantization (10% -> 50% -> 100%).

Bench plan asks from BrightForge:
- Provide anonymized sample prompts + a 24-hr representative traffic CSV.
- Confirm whether session affinity is required beyond 30 minutes.

I'll queue the micro-bench today once we have the prompt set.

Karthik
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: BrightForge post-call: deployment synthesis, SLO targets & next steps — POC scope & timeline

Laura — attached is the one-page POC scope (see bf-slo-matrix-20281009.xlsx) and the network sketch (bf-network-topology.png). TL;DR POC plan and timeline: 

- Week 0 (today–Oct 16): exchange sample prompts & trace; Redwood produces a detailed POC runbook and cost estimate.
- Week 1 (Oct 17–24): bench runs (low/mid/high) + latency and cost collection; quick once-per-day sync.
- Week 2 (Oct 25–31): validation against SLOs, fallback test, and ops runbook handoff.

Deliverables: benchmark report, SLO matrix populated with measured numbers, recommended Dedicated config, and SOC2 evidence pointer for procurement.

Action items assigned: 
- BrightForge: share prompts + traffic trace by Oct 11 (Laura).
- Redwood: run micro-bench and share initial numbers by Oct 18 (Karthik).
- Redwood Sales/Ops: prepare procurement packet and draft contract template for Dedicated (Connor / Naomi).

Naomi — can you prepare a short procurement packet we can attach to the HubSpot deal? Monica — looping you for initial estimated commit options (4-node baseline / flexible burst).

Connor

- SOC2: we will provide SOC2 Type II report and an infra control summary within 2 business days of request.
- Data residency: Dedicated in us-west available; can sign region clause.
- Contract: draft MSA + Dedicated addendum (sample provided).
- Pricing: Monica will send two commit tiers (Baseline 4-node, Baseline + Burst).

Laura — once you confirm the sample prompt handoff, we'll attach the procurement packet to the HubSpot deal and kick off legal redlines. Looking forward to your prompts.

Best,
